product.summary: Hoplite is a platform that lets developers run multiple AI coding agents in the cloud. Each agent reads, modifies, and tests code in an isolated development environment, checks browser previews, and eventually creates GitHub pull requests.
product.problem_statement: Running multiple AI coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, Codex) simultaneously on a local laptop slows down or crashes the machine, and closing the laptop interrupts progress. Cloud solutions are complex to set up and create platform lock-in.
product.solution: Hoplite provides a cloud-based agent execution environment that works immediately after connecting a GitHub repository and setting up dependencies. It can import existing local configurations (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.), and each thread persists with its own independent workspace.
key_features: Run agents instantly after connecting a GitHub repository
Isolated dev environment per thread (vCPU 2, 8GiB RAM)
Supports multiple models including Claude Code and Codex on a single platform
Agents can view and work in a browser preview directly
Persistent state allows continuing work in the same thread after review feedback
MCP server integration and prompt submission via iMessage
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Runs AI agents in cloud-based sandbox environments, continuously preserving each agent's work history and state. Offers flexibility to mix multiple AI models without requiring users to set up separate infrastructure.
product.target_customer: Software development teams, especially small to medium-sized startups and developers looking to actively leverage AI coding agents.
product.business_model: Freemium premium subscription model. The free tier allows up to 5 agents; paid plans are monthly per seat with additional usage.

direct_competitors.comparison: Single AI coding agent tool that runs locally, with no built-in multi-agent orchestration or cloud infrastructure.
AI-powered code editor but focused on local execution, lacking cloud capabilities for running multiple agents simultaneously.
Specializes in code autocomplete and chat; agents do not autonomously perform tasks.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Hoplite focuses on infrastructure for running multiple AI coding agents simultaneously in the cloud. Users can operate several agents like Claude Code and Codex in one environment without being locked into a specific model, and seamlessly migrate local setups to the cloud.
competitive_landscape.moat: Signal from Stripe founders and Paul Graham as direct investors, YC Summer 2026 batch participation, early user traction (processed 824B tokens, 18,000 users), fast product development pace.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Hoplite is pioneering a new category in the AI coding agent market: multi-agent orchestration. While existing tools focus on single agents, Hoplite aims to become the infrastructure for agent teams.

trending_reason.summary: The $5.5M seed round led by Stripe founders and Paul Graham validates market interest in AI coding agent infrastructure. As AI coding agent usage surged in 2026, the need for efficient cloud infrastructure to operate them has grown.
catalysts: Rising infrastructure demand driven by the popularization of AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.)
Increased market credibility from a Stripe founder-led investment
Fast growth in the Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch
trending_reason.growth_metrics: Processed 824B tokens and acquired 18,000 users since launch (per independent reporting, 2026-11-21)

funding.total_raised_note: Only the Seed round has been disclosed. No additional grants or loans identified.

funding_history.note: Seed round with participation from the Stripe brothers and Paul Graham

market_outlook.tam_sam_som: The AI developer tools market is growing rapidly as of 2026, with coding agents expected to capture a significant share of the overall development workflow. TAM is estimated to be in the billions of dollars, though exact figures are not confirmed.
market_outlook.market_trend: As AI coding agent usage explodes, demand for infrastructure that efficiently manages and runs multiple agents is increasing. Not only large enterprises but also small teams are adopting AI agents.
market_outlook.growth_potential: With improving AI model performance and declining costs, more development teams are expected to shift to agent-based development. As an early market entrant, Hoplite has an opportunity to build strong network effects.
risks: Risk of major cloud providers (AWS, GCP) launching similar services
Possibility of AI model companies (Anthropic, OpenAI) expanding their own infrastructure
Security and data privacy concerns (code repository access permissions, etc.)
As an early-stage startup, customer acquisition and continuous product development are needed
market_outlook.risk_mitigation: Avoids lock-in to specific model providers through multi-model support, leverages backing from YC and prominent investors, and runs a fast product improvement cycle based on early user feedback.

hoplite-2026.editor_pick_comment: An AI coding agent infrastructure directly invested in by Stripe founders and Paul Graham, solving the practical problem of 'your laptop crashing when running multiple agents locally.'

product.summary: Kindo is an 'AI Control Center' platform that enables enterprise IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance teams to discover, observe, control, and audit all AI users, chatbots, and agents running across their organization in one place.
product.problem_statement: As AI agents proliferate by the thousands inside enterprises, autonomous tasks such as data access, modifying customer records, and changing production systems have increased. However, IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance teams lack a central view of which agents are operating where, with what permissions, and at what cost. Shadow AI emerges, and the same agents frequently expose sensitive data or violate policies.
product.solution: Kindo uses a turnkey approach: simply connect to existing infrastructure to automatically discover all AI agents. It then consolidates all agent activity, access, costs, and outcomes into a single dashboard, and allows IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance teams to set control policies (what they can do, which data they can access, budget limits, etc.) tailored to each team's permissions. A gateway governs and audits all API calls, and offers a 'Harness' feature for human intervention when needed.
key_features: Automatic AI agent discovery and shadow AI mapping
Observe all agent activity, access, costs, and outcomes from a single command center
Identity-based access control (integrated with existing enterprise permissions)
Per-agent token consumption and execution result recording, plus budget and limit setting
Real-time monitoring, alerts, and hard spending caps
SOC/NOC-style intervention (including agent takeover functionality)
Air-gapped on-premises deployment support (Kindo Deep Hat model)
Compliant with SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, NIST CSF
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Kindo Deep Hat: A proprietary suite of cybersecurity AI models that run on-premises on enterprise GPUs.
product.target_customer: Large enterprises and mid-sized companies in financial services, professional services, healthcare, aviation, and transportation (e.g., global aviation data provider Aireon)
product.business_model: Custom pricing (quote after demo); various deployment options: cloud/SaaS, private cloud/VPC, on-premises, air-gapped

Raised $20M seed in June 2026; specialized in agent governance. Narrower scope of discovery and cost management compared to Kindo.
Raised $125M Series C in August 2026; focused on AI agent security. Lacks integrated control across four departments compared to Kindo.
In security operations automation; competes with Kindo, but Kindo has an edge with air-gapped deployments for aviation and defense customers.
Security operations automation; less specialized in AI agent management than Kindo.
IT operations automation; lacks cost and governance features compared to Kindo.

Also the only platform that includes per-agent cost tracking (run-level recording) and runtime intervention (agent takeover).
competitive_landscape.moat: 1) Industry network and compliance expertise from founder with three unicorn CISO roles; 2) Diverse deployment options including air-gapped and on-premises; 3) Proprietary Deep Hat models; 4) 800% YoY revenue growth with reference customers in finance, healthcare, and aviation.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: The AI agent management market is growing rapidly with many startups emerging, but Kindo positions itself as the only vendor that meets the needs of four departments in a single platform. The 800% growth rate and over $57M raised indicate early market leadership.

stryx-ai-2026.tagline: A defense startup providing low-cost drone interception systems for military and critical infrastructure.

founders.background: Graduate of École Polytechnique. Co-founder of French marketing SaaS unicorn Brevo (formerly Sendinblue).
founders.notable_achievement: Brevo became a unicorn in December 2025 with a valuation exceeding €1B. Stryx AI is Thiberge’s second startup.

product.summary: Stryx AI develops an integrated counter-drone system combining a low-cost radar, 'Stryx Watch', and an autonomous interceptor drone, 'Stryx Impact'. Targets include fiber-optic-guided FPV drones that cannot be jammed by existing electronic warfare.
product.problem_statement: You can’t use multi-million-euro missiles to intercept small drones (FPVs, Shaheds, etc.) costing hundreds of euros, and electronic jamming is ineffective against fiber-optic-guided drones. There is a critical need for a low-cost physical interception solution that reliably neutralizes drones.
product.solution: The self-developed radar detects and tracks targets, and an AI-based autonomous interceptor drone destroys them via kinetic collision. The entire process is automated under a human-in-the-loop launch command.
key_features: Stryx Watch: Compact, lightweight, portable drone detection radar (ground or vehicle-mounted).
Stryx Impact: AI-guided autonomous interceptor drone (capable of striking FPVs, Shahed-class medium-to-large drones).
Stryx C2: Command-and-control software integrating the entire ecosystem (real-time threat visualization, radar operation, interceptor launch control).
Stryx Launch: Automated launcher that stores and deploys multiple interceptors.
Operated under human command to reduce the risk of accidental engagement.
Open architecture allows integration with third-party defense systems.
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: AI-based autonomous navigation and target identification; kinetic interceptor approach; can counter fiber-optic-guided drones; provides reliable physical neutralization even where jamming is ineffective.
product.target_customer: European militaries (especially the French Army and Defense Innovation Agency), critical infrastructure operators (airports, power plants, borders), and defense primes (MBDA, Thales, etc.) as a subcontractor for interceptor systems.
product.business_model: Equipment sales (radar, interceptor, launcher, software) + maintenance and operations contracts. Targets site-level integrated solution packages rather than individual equipment sales.

direct_competitors.comparison: Interceptor BLAZE selected by the French Army. Entered production phase 5 months ahead of Stryx AI.
Has the GOBI interceptor; already secured delivery contracts with DGA under other programs (5,000 DELCO drones).

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Interception cost designed to be comparable to the target drone's price (disruptive pricing strategy). Can counter fiber-optic-guided FPV drones. The founder’s background in SaaS success rather than defense is a contrarian investment angle.

Stryx AI entered the latest, but is attempting a fast catch-up by building its own production line with a €7.7M seed round. The outcome hinges on price competitiveness and relationships with military procurement officials.

The Ukraine war has proven the power of small FPV drones, triggering a surge in urgent demand from European militaries and a boom in European counter-drone startup investment since 2024.
catalysts: The routine use of low-cost FPV drones to disable tanks and artillery in the Ukraine war has dramatically increased demand for counter-drone interception systems.
Existing jamming systems proven ineffective against fiber-optic-guided drones.
The French Defense Innovation Agency (AID) is testing Stryx AI prototypes under a rapid-response program (September 2026 XLAD joint exercise).
EU-level discussions on joint procurement for critical infrastructure protection (PERePO) are ongoing.

market_outlook.growth_potential: France is preparing a multi-billion-euro new counter-drone system procurement under the PARADE program successor. EU member states are also discussing joint procurement, offering significant growth potential.
risks: Competitors (Origin Robotics/DSV) already selected as French Army suppliers, with a lead of over 5 months.
